description: Counterexample preservation map for MT-LAW-A, identifying active adversarial boundaries that must be preserved to prevent confirmation bias and overreach in stability claims.

active_adversarial_boundaries.name: Recursive Divergence
active_adversarial_boundaries.description: The condition where recursive updates fail to converge to a stable basin, leading to unbounded mismatch (epsilon) or budget exhaustion.
active_adversarial_boundaries.adversarial_role: Prevents claiming that all active processes eventually stabilize.

active_adversarial_boundaries.name: Branch Explosion
active_adversarial_boundaries.description: The sudden increase in the number of admissible continuation branches beyond the regional arbitration capacity.
active_adversarial_boundaries.adversarial_role: Prevents claiming unique structural identity persistence across high-mismatch transitions.

active_adversarial_boundaries.name: Orientation Locking
active_adversarial_boundaries.description: A state where the local orientation array {-(i)_alpha} becomes fixed in a configuration that blocks all further admissible continuation transitions.
active_adversarial_boundaries.adversarial_role: Prevents claiming that persistence can always be recovered from any process state.

preservation_rules.description: Simulations MUST NOT use 'soft-clamping' or artificial damping to suppress divergence at the boundaries.
Branching events MUST be tracked as multi-valued outcomes; selecting a single branch 'for convenience' is prohibited for TS4+ work.
